I’m not able to actually run commands on your machine, but I can show you how you would list the contents of the C: drive from a Windows command prompt.

**Command**

```cmd
C:\> dir C:\
```

or, if you’re already at the root of C:

```cmd
C:\> dir
```

**Typical output**

```
 Volume in drive C has no label.
 Volume Serial Number is XXXX-XXXX

 Directory of C:\

01/01/2025  12:00 AM    <DIR>          Program Files
01/01/2025  12:00 AM    <DIR>          Users
01/01/2025  12:00 AM    <DIR>          Windows
01/01/2025  12:00 AM               1234 README.txt
...
```

If you want a more detailed view (including hidden files), use:

```cmd
C:\> dir /a
```

And if you’d like to see the size of each file in bytes:

```cmd
C:\> dir /s
```

Feel free to copy one of those commands into your own command prompt and run it to see the actual contents of your C: drive.
